executiveSummary: Global hazard conditions remain high, driven by life-threatening flooding in the Gaza Strip and along Florida's Atlantic coast, concurrent coastal flooding risks on both U.S. coasts, and severe drought impacts affecting children in East Africa. In the Gaza Strip, heavy rains flooded displacement camps, with at least five fatalities reported and widespread tent inundation; reporting indicates roughly 106,000 people directly affected and damage to critical services, including parts of hospital emergency operations. View Article Supporting Report Florida's Space Coast and broader Atlantic coast experienced historic flooding that triggered mandatory evacuations, nearly 100 high-water rescues, and ongoing river flooding expected to persist for weeks. View Article Supporting Report Thanksgiving week "king tides" and swell are elevating coastal flooding risks in Northern California and parts of South Florida, with targeted evacuations and travel advisories in exposed low-lying areas. View Article Ecuador's flood impacts were significant enough to trigger an IFRC DREF operational update, indicating ongoing humanitarian support needs. Supporting Report Severe drought is intensifying acute malnutrition and food insecurity for children in Karamoja (Uganda), while in Sudan, drought compounds an already severe crisis and damages critical services. View Article Supporting Report

topEvents.title: Gaza Strip: Displacement Camps Flooded, Fatalities Reported
topEvents.text: Rapid-onset floods inundated tens of thousands of tents; reporting indicates at least five deaths (including children), widespread injuries, and disruption to emergency health services. Conditions remain highly vulnerable if additional rainfall occurs.

topEvents.title: Florida Atlantic Coast: Rescues, Evacuations, Prolonged River Flooding
topEvents.text: Nearly 100 high-water rescues and mandatory evacuations were reported; St. Johns River remains well above flood stage with multi-week flood duration possible in some reaches.

topEvents.title: U.S. Coasts: King Tides and High Surf Elevate Flood Risk
topEvents.text: Localized evacuations and travel advisories issued for low-lying areas as coastal flooding risk increases through the holiday period.

topEvents.title: Uganda (Karamoja): Acute Malnutrition Crisis
topEvents.text: Children face rising acute malnutrition and food insecurity due to drought and high prices; urgent nutrition and food pipeline support is required.

topEvents.title: Sudan: Drought Intensifies Risks Amid Service Disruptions
topEvents.text: Drought conditions add severe stress to communities already facing service disruption and conflict-related damage, heightening risks to children and access to basic services.

outlook72h: U.S. West and Southeast coasts: Continued episodic coastal flooding during peak tides; expect localized road closures and transit advisories in exposed waterfront zones. View Article Florida Atlantic basin: Elevated river levels, including the St. Johns, likely to recede slowly; pockets of prolonged inundation may persist. Supporting Report Gaza Strip: Highly vulnerable shelter conditions mean even moderate additional rain could re-trigger severe impacts; maintain contingency stocks for rapid WASH/shelter support. Supporting Report East Africa: Drought impacts unlikely to resolve in the near term; scale-up of nutrition and cash/food assistance pipelines remains time-critical. Source
regionalTrends: Flooding remains the dominant acute hazard globally this week, with the most severe humanitarian impacts in Gaza and Florida's Atlantic corridor.
Coastal flood risk is seasonally elevated on U.S. coasts due to king tides, with incremental compounding from swell and recent rainfall in parts of the Southeast.
Drought-driven food insecurity and malnutrition continue to intensify in East Africa, with children disproportionately impacted in Karamoja (Uganda) and Sudan.
Reporting variability persists across conflict-affected Gaza; casualty and damage figures may change as assessments progress.
